author.name: A.R. Pyx
bio: I write historical fiction for readers who want adventure with real weight: hidden histories, moral pressure, and characters forced to act when the world begins to tilt.
I’m drawn to periods of transition, so far the 1890s and the 1930s, when old certainties break apart and ordinary people must decide what they are willing to protect, betray, or become.

I’m an archaeologist, and my fiction grows out of the same questions as the day job: where documented history ends, where imagination begins, and how each can shape the other. The research in the novels is real; the trouble the characters get into is mine.

I explore that restless spirit through different lenses:
  • Hic Non Sunt Dracones, a Victorian-era novella in the King Solomon’s Mines tradition.
  • Echoes of Lost Worlds, a 1930s archaeological adventure series indebted to Indiana Jones. Its first book, 1934: Caught in the Crossroads, returns in a revised edition on November 22, 2026.
  • More still ahead: a science-fiction entry, a cozy mystery, and a contemporary story, each chasing what people risk in pursuit of what’s been lost.

1934: Caught in the Crossroads is my debut novel. It stands on its own, but it also opens the door to a wider fictional world rooted in real places, real tensions, and the enduring human habit of chasing meaning through the ruins.
